analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including file metadata, both ClusterServiceCommand revisions, and the bounded StartCommand+ClusterMember patch. ClusterServiceCommand.swift:89-116 now enables coordinated updates using Watchdog settings and wires request/progress files, live pair updates and candidate recovery into the supervisor. ClusterMemberSupervisor.swift:466-527 starts one background cycle, binds its restart callback to the current child, and cancels/awaits the cycle after child exit; :156-176 and :589-613 add pre-reexec start checks and recovery. Existing operator-stop and restart-budget behavior remains visible. No independently supported security regression was established in this scope.
Relevant contracts are provider availability (A-018), operator/process isolation (TB-003), rollback authority (T-043), signed-build qualification (A-017/T-054), and connection-bound authorization (T-053). The supplied changes do not directly modify encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing or attestation verification.
Integration must inspect ClusterPairUpdateCycle and ClusterCandidateRecovery: authenticated peer/drain coordination, bounded cancellation, update leases, release/predecessor verification and quarantine enforcement are delegated, not demonstrated missing here. Verify that the StartCommand+ClusterMember drain flag is enabled only for the intended paired route and remains subject to current serving authorization; its patch is truncated and only metadata is supplied as a primary unit. Candidate promotion at ClusterMemberSupervisor.swift:551-552 uses PID/version/freshness but not serving phase; ClusterServiceCommand.swift:211-236 emits an independent process-alive heartbeat. Confirm that recovery intentionally measures service stability rather than successful inference and that rollback/start-check refusal paths cannot create persistent restart failures. These material update/drain contracts require the next source/integration pass; no full-PR clearance is implied.
